structure: Part 10, Upload documents and delete a document. Read in full at commit c2078fb (the checkout's HEAD): app/views/design-release-2.1/upload-documents.html (251 lines: phase banner and back link, notification-status partial, caption and heading, intro copy, a bulleted list of other documents, a details component with a consignment/documents-needed table and a GOV.UK link, then one form holding the error summary, a 'File upload' card with four fields (document reference input, document type select, date of issue MOJ date picker, attachment file drop zone with a requirements list), a 'Save and add another' button, the uploaded-documents table with status tags and a Remove link per row, and the shared journey-form-actions partial); app/views/design-release-2.1/delete-document.html (26 lines: phase banner, back link, journey two-thirds layout, default page name and confirm text, the delete-confirmation partial); app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/delete-confirmation.html (31 lines: heading, inset or paragraph confirm text, summary list, 'This action cannot be undone.', a form with 'Yes, delete' and 'No, cancel'); app/routes.js 12412-12684 (document type options and labels, select items, uploaded documents list and display statuses, body parsing, validateUploadDocument, add, mark virus check passed, remove, form-state reset, trySavePendingUploadDocument, return query, renderUploadDocumentsPage); app/routes.js 13993-14128 (GET and POST /upload-documents/:documentId/delete, GET /upload-documents, POST /upload-documents/virus-check/:documentId, POST /upload-documents with remove, add-another, hub/review soft save, continue and fallback branches). To say where each action leads, also read the helpers these call: app/routes.js 300-349 (testing and Round 2 flags, usesHealthCertificateWording), 1725-1824 (journey steps around /upload-documents, getNextJourneyPath, isJourneySoftSaveAction, getJourneySaveRedirect, getSectionContinueRedirect), 5193-5199 and 7088-7090 and 7173-7185 (how the delete summary formats a blank value), app/views/layouts/journey.html, and app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html for the bottom buttons. Those are claimed only as they bear on these pages; their own parts own them. The client-side virus-check and drop-zone scripts in app/assets/ are out of scope and were not read. Covered: the upload page's route, back link, caption, heading, all copy, every field with its label, hint and options (13 document types), the uploaded-documents table with its two statuses and the Remove link, all six validation messages, the virus-check endpoint, and where add-another, save and return to overview, save and return, save and continue and the fallback each lead; the delete-document page's route, heading, inset text, four summary rows, warning, 'Yes, delete' and 'No, cancel' and where each leads. Changed since the earlier extract (at 04a073b): the intro now says 'health certificate' instead of ITAHC, Remove is now a link to the new delete-document confirmation page instead of an immediate delete, and the soft save on Save and continue or Save and return now validates a pending document when any field is filled, not only when a type is chosen. Stops at review.

claims.statement: The upload documents page is served at /upload-documents; under Design Release 2.1 it is reached at /design-release-2.1/upload-documents because the version mount copies every root route under that prefix.
claims.note: The /design-release-2.1 prefix comes from app/lib/version-mount.js, which another part reads.

claims.statement: In the linear journey the upload documents page comes after the transporter page and before roles and addresses.
When the user is creating a template in Design Release 2.1, the upload documents page is left out of the journey steps.
Opening the upload documents page while creating a template in Design Release 2.1 redirects to the notification hub instead of showing the page.
Submitting the upload documents form while creating a template in Design Release 2.1 redirects to the notification hub without saving anything.
Opening the upload documents page ensures the notification has a reference, and the page shows the notification reference, falling back to the prototype's default reference.
Opening the upload documents page clears any earlier errors and any half-entered document reference, type, date of issue and attachment, so the form always opens empty.

claims.statement: The page shows the Alpha phase banner with a feedback-by-email link.
The page has a Back link.
The Back link goes to the review page when the user came from review or is amending the notification, and otherwise to the notification hub.
The page shows the notification status block above the heading.
claims.note: The notification-status partial's own content is claimed by the shell part.

claims.statement: The page caption is 'Documents'.
The page heading is 'Upload documents', which is also the page name.
The intro tells the user they must attach a health certificate if the consignment requires one and can add it later if they do not have it now.
claims.quote: You must attach an health certificate if this consignment requires one. If you do not have it now, you can add it later.
claims.note: Replaces the earlier wording 'You must attach an ITAHC'. The source keeps the article 'an' before 'health certificate', a typo. In Design Release 2.1 the document type list still names the first option 'Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC)', so the intro and the list use different names for the certificate.

claims.statement: The intro tells the user all documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port.
claims.quote: All documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port.

claims.statement: The intro tells the user documents must be in English and every page must be uploaded.

claims.statement: The date of issue field is a Ministry of Justice date picker component, not the GOV.UK three-box date input.
The date of issue has no rule about being in the past or relative to the arrival date; it only has to be a real date.
claims.note: validateUploadDocument checks only presence and parseArrivalDisplayDate; no future-date or range rule exists.

claims.statement: The fourth field is labelled 'Attachment' with the hint 'Your file must be:'.
claims.quote:

claims.statement: The attachment hint says files must be smaller than 50MB.
The attachment hint says the allowed file types are PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX.
claims.quote: • PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX

claims.statement: The attachment hint says up to a maximum of 15 files can be uploaded.
The attachment hint says ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons.
claims.quote: • ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons

claims.statement: The prototype does not enforce the 50MB size limit, the allowed file types or the ZIP ban on the server: no validation checks them.
claims.note: validateUploadDocument checks only the file count, reference, type, date and that a file name is present. No error message exists for a too-large file, a wrong type or a ZIP.

claims.statement: The attachment is a drop zone showing the chosen file name, or 'No file chosen', with a 'Choose file' control and the text 'or drop file'.

claims.statement: The file status line in the drop zone is announced to screen readers as it changes.
The prototype does not upload the file itself: the server records only the chosen file name, sent in a hidden attachmentFileName field.
claims.note: The form has no multipart encoding and the handlers read only body.attachmentFileName; the drop-zone script that fills the hidden field is client-side and out of scope.

claims.statement: On a validation error the page keeps what the user typed in document reference, document type, date of issue and the attachment file name.
Each field shows its own error message beside it, and the attachment field and drop zone take an error style when the attachment is in error.
A 'Save and add another' button below the fields saves the document entered and returns to the same page.

claims.statement: Saving and adding another keeps the ?from=review or ?from=hub return context; amending a notification always counts as coming from review.
Save and add another validates every field; when all pass, the document is added to the list and the form is cleared.
A blank document reference shows the error 'Enter a document reference', linked to the reference field. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed first.
No document type, or a value not in the list, shows the error 'Select a document type', linked to the type field.

claims.quote: errors.dateOfIssue = { text: 'Enter a date of issue' }

claims.statement: A date of issue that cannot be read as a real date shows the error 'Enter a real date', linked to the date field.

} else if (!parseArrivalDisplayDate(values.dateOfIssue)) {

claims.note: The date is parsed with the same parser as the arrival date picker (parseArrivalDisplayDate), which another part reads.

claims.statement: No chosen file shows the error 'Upload a document', linked to the attachment field.
Errors for the reference, type, date and attachment are reported together, in that order, in the error summary.
claims.note: Each check pushes to errorList in sequence without returning early, so all failures show at once.

claims.statement: A notification can hold at most 15 documents.
Saving a document when 15 are already listed shows only the error 'You can upload a maximum of 15 files', linked to the attachment field, and checks nothing else.
claims.quote:
if (uploadedCount >= MAX_UPLOADED_DOCUMENTS) {

claims.statement: Each saved document records its reference, type, type label, date of issue, file name, a virus status of 'uploading' and when it was added.

claims.statement: Saved documents are kept in the notification's session data as a list of uploaded documents.
The date of issue is stored as the text the user entered, not as a normalised date.
claims.note: parseArrivalDisplayDate is used only to validate; the trimmed raw string is saved and shown in the table and on the delete page.

claims.statement: When at least one document is saved, a table lists them below the 'Save and add another' button with the columns Document reference, Document type, Date of issue, Status and a visually hidden 'Action' column.

claims.statement: With no saved documents, no table is shown.
Each row shows the document reference, the document type's display label and the date of issue as entered.

claims.statement: A document of type itahc is labelled 'Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC)' and one of type health-certificate is labelled 'Health certificate'; an unknown type shows its raw value.
claims.note: mechanism: picks the display label for a saved document's type. The table shows the label stored when the document was saved, falling back to this lookup (getUploadedDocumentTypeLabel, app/routes.js:12467-12473).

claims.statement: A newly saved document's status shows as a blue 'Scanning for virus' tag.
claims.quote:
text: document.virusStatus === 'passed' ? 'Check completed' : 'Scanning for virus',
      class: document.virusStatus === 'passed' ? 'govuk-tag--green' : 'govuk-tag--blue'

claims.statement: Once its virus check has passed, a document's status shows as a green 'Check completed' tag.
The status cell carries visually hidden text 'Virus check status for' followed by the document reference.
The virus check has only two outcomes, scanning and passed; there is no failed or infected status and no message for a file that fails the check.
claims.note: Statuses are 'uploading' and 'passed' only; looked in getUploadedDocumentsForDisplay and markUploadedDocumentVirusCheckPassed.

claims.statement: A POST to /upload-documents/virus-check/{documentId} marks that document's virus check as passed if it is still scanning, and answers with JSON giving its virus status, or null if no such document exists.

The virus check is simulated: the page asks the server to mark each scanning document as passed after a 2.5 second delay, so the tag changes from 'Scanning for virus' to 'Check completed' without a real scan.
claims.note: The server constant is unused in routes.js; the status tag carries data-virus-status and data-document-id for a client script (in app/assets, out of scope, not read) that calls the virus-check endpoint. The rendered traces cover the client behaviour.

claims.statement: Each row of the uploaded documents table has a 'Remove' link.
claims.note: Replaces the earlier 'Remove' submit button, which deleted the document straight away.

claims.statement: The Remove link carries visually hidden text naming the document reference, so screen reader users hear which document it removes.
The Remove link goes to the delete-document confirmation page for that document, at /upload-documents/{document id}/delete under the journey's base path, keeping ?from=review or ?from=hub.
claims.quote: href="{{ (journeyBasePath + '/upload-documents') if journeyBasePath else '/upload-documents' }}/{{ document.id }}/delete{% if fromReview %}?from=review{% elif fromHub %}?from=hub{% endif %}"

claims.statement: Following the Remove link leaves the upload page without saving anything typed in the form fields, so a half-entered document is lost.
claims.note: Remove is now a plain link, not a form submit, so the pending fields are not posted; deleting and returning to the page both reset the form state.

claims.statement: The upload form handler still deletes a document straight away for a 'remove:{document id}' action, clearing the form and reloading the page with its return context, but no control on the page now sends that action.
claims.note: mechanism: a leftover branch for the old Remove button; the view's Remove is a link to the delete-document page and no button has a remove: value.

claims.statement: The delete-document page is served at /upload-documents/{document id}/delete; under Design Release 2.1 it is reached at /design-release-2.1/upload-documents/{document id}/delete because the version mount copies every root route under that prefix.
claims.note: The /design-release-2.1 prefix comes from app/lib/version-mount.js, which another part reads.

claims.statement: Opening the delete-document page for a document that does not exist redirects back to the upload documents page, keeping the review or hub return context.
The delete-document page shows the Alpha phase banner with a feedback-by-email link.
The delete-document page has a Back link to the upload documents page, keeping the review or hub return context.
The delete-document page sits in the standard two-thirds column journey layout and shows no caption and no notification status block.
claims.note: Neither the view nor the delete-confirmation partial includes a caption or the notification-status partial, unlike the upload documents page.

claims.statement: The delete-document page heading is 'Delete this document?', which is also the page name.
Below the heading, inset text says 'This will remove the document from this notification.'
claims.quote: confirmText: 'This will remove the document from this notification.',

claims.statement: A summary list shows the document being deleted in four rows: Document reference, Document type, Date of issue and File.
claims.quote:
buildDeleteSummaryRow('Document reference', document.documentReference),
      buildDeleteSummaryRow('Document type', document.documentTypeLabel || getDocumentTypeLabel(document.documentType, req.session.data)),
      buildDeleteSummaryRow('Date of issue', document.dateOfIssue),
      buildDeleteSummaryRow('File', document.fileName)

claims.statement: The summary's Document type row shows the label saved with the document, or looks the label up from the type when none was saved; the File row shows the chosen file name and the Date of issue row shows the date as entered.
A blank value in the delete summary shows as 'Not applicable'.
claims.note: mechanism: formats each delete-summary value. A saved document always has every field, so this shows only for data that skipped validation.

claims.statement: Below the summary the page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
The page has a red warning button 'Yes, delete' that posts to /upload-documents/{document id}/delete, keeping the review or hub return context.
claims.note: The form action is deleteAction: `/upload-documents/${encodeURIComponent(documentId)}/delete${returnQuery}`.

claims.statement: Beside the button, a 'No, cancel' link goes back to the upload documents page without deleting, keeping the review or hub return context.
Pressing 'Yes, delete' removes the document from the notification, clears the upload form and returns to the upload documents page, keeping the review or hub return context.
Confirming the delete of a document that no longer exists does nothing and still returns to the upload documents page.
The delete-document page and its delete action have no guard for template creation, unlike the upload documents page, which sends a template-creating user to the hub.
claims.note: Looked in both delete handlers for isDesignRelease21TemplateCreate; neither checks it. Templates have no documents to delete, so the page is unreachable from the journey in that state.

claims.statement: The page ends with the shared journey buttons: by default 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link.
claims.note: The partial's amend and template-review variants are claimed by the shell part; this page passes no options.

claims.statement: Uploading documents is optional: Save and continue, or Save and return to overview, with every document field left empty moves on without any error.

If anything is entered in any document field (a file, a reference, a date or a type) when the user presses Save and continue or a save-and-return button, every document field is validated; with errors the page is shown again with them, and if all pass the document is saved before moving on.
claims.note: Replaces the earlier rule that validated only once a document type was chosen and silently discarded other partial entries. The code comment at 14103-14104 still describes the old rule ('once a document type is chosen').

claims.statement: With 15 documents already listed, entering anything in the form and pressing Save and continue or a save-and-return button shows the 'You can upload a maximum of 15 files' error instead of moving on.
claims.note: trySavePendingUploadDocument runs the same validateUploadDocument as Save and add another, whose first check is the file count.

claims.statement: Save and continue goes to the next journey step, roles and addresses, unless the user came from the hub (back to the hub), from review (back to review) or from a template review (save and return to that template).
Save and return to overview, and Save and return when amending, apply the same optional-upload validation, save the draft notification, and go to the hub or review respectively.
Any other submission clears the form and goes to the notification hub.
On this page only Save and return to overview and Save and return (amend) explicitly save the draft notification; Save and add another, Remove and Save and continue do not call the draft save.
claims.note: persistDraftNotification is called in getJourneySaveRedirect, used only by the hub/review branch; the add-another branch and the delete-document handler redirect without it. Whether continue persists depends on getSectionContinueRedirect, which does not call it.
